summary.one_liner: Aperant (formerly Auto Claude) is an Electron desktop app that runs multiple AI agents to plan, build, and self-validate coding tasks in isolated git worktrees, currently in maintenance mode while a 3.0 rewrite is underway.
summary.what_it_does: The app lets you open a git repository, describe a task, and have agents plan, implement, and validate the work autonomously. Changes happen in git worktrees so the main branch stays untouched, and up to 12 agent terminals can run in parallel. It includes a self-validating QA loop, AI-assisted merge conflict resolution when integrating back to main, and a memory layer that keeps insights across sessions. It also offers GitHub/GitLab issue import and merge request creation, Linear task sync, a Kanban board, an Insights chat for exploring the codebase, Ideation for finding improvements and vulnerabilities, and changelog generation from completed tasks. The README describes a three-layer security model: OS sandbox, filesystem restrictions to the project directory, and a dynamic command allowlist based on the detected project stack.
use_cases: Autonomously implementing a feature from a plain-language description
Running several coding tasks in parallel with isolated branches
Importing GitHub or GitLab issues and having AI investigate them
Syncing development tasks with Linear for team progress tracking
Generating release notes from completed tasks
Reviewing and merging agent-generated changes safely
notable: Parallel agent execution with up to 12 terminals, each in its own git worktree
Self-validating QA loop and AI-powered merge conflict resolution
Memory layer that carries insights across sessions
Three-layer security model with OS sandbox, filesystem limits, and dynamic command allowlist
caveats: Pull requests are paused during the 3.0 rebuild; code PRs against the current app will be closed
The 2.x desktop app is in maintenance mode, so new features are going into 3.0 with no public release date
Requires a Claude Pro/Max subscription and the Claude Code CLI, and the project must be a git repository
keywords: run multiple ai coding tasks at once
